identificationModule.briefTitle: Efficacy of Methyl Aminolevulinate + Daylight in Patients With Facial Photodamage
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Double-blind Randomized-controlled Trial to Assess the Efficacy of Methyl Aminolevulinate + Daylight vs Placebo + Daylight in Patients With Facial Photodamage

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Treatment of actinic damage has included multiple procedures but to date there is limited scientific evidence to support the preferential use of one of these therapies according to their efficacy, safety and pain tolerance by patients. This study aims to assess the efficacy of methyl aminolevulinate + daylight vs placebo + daylight to treat facial photodamage

armGroups.label: Methyl Aminolevulinate (MAL)
armGroups.description: 1 gram of Topical Methyl Aminolevulinate (MAL) applied to the whole face 30 minutes before sun exposure for 2 hours (3 sessions , 2 to 4 weeks apart)

armGroups.label: Placebo
armGroups.description: 1 gram of placebo cream applied to the whole face 30 minutes before sun exposure for 2 hours (3 sessions , 2 to 4 weeks apart)

primaryOutcomes.description: The primary outcome is global photodamage improvement 1 month after the third daylight PDT session, according to Dover´s photodamage scale.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Pain evaluation with the visual analogue scale after 2 hours of sun exposure in each of the sessions performed (Sessions 1, 2 and 3).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: After 2 hours of sun exposure in each session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Specific photodamage severity score for fine lines, coarse lines, tactile roughness, mottled pigmentation, sallowness, and erythema one month after the third daylight PDT session, according to Dover´s photodamage scale.
Sun irradiation and illuminance quantification during exposure
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During the 2 hours of each session
From recruitment until 1 month after the third session

secondaryOutcomes.description: Therapy tolerance will be recorded with a scale that includes a 4-grade severity score for oozing, erythema, oedema, desquamation, pigmentation, and vesiculation.

secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Basal and 1 month after the third session

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults with symmetric facial photodamage grade 2 or 3 (Dover´s scale)
* Patients willing to participate
* Signed informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pregnant or nursing females
* Subjects with any photosensitizing disorder
* Any active infectious skin disorder
* History of herpes simplex in the face
* Subjects with less than 6 months of any previous rejuvenation interfering treatments
* History of systemic isotretinoin in the last year
* Subjects requiring concurrent treatment that would interfere with study objectives and/or assessments
* History of hypersensitivity reactions
* Activities with high sun exposure during 48 hours after treatment
* Clinical suspicion of any systemic or local malignancy
